title: Fundamentals of Accounting
description: Accounting for the people who run storage sites, in storage words: the equation and the accounts, debits and credits, cash and accrual, how rent and fees are earned, receivables and bad debt, fixed assets and depreciation, payables, cards and the bank, the close and the three statements, budgets, controls and the audit. Course 8 of the Academy, for managers and the accounting team's new hires.
overview: Why the numbers matter and where a site's numbers come from
The accounting equation, the five kinds of account and the chart
Debits and credits, with six storage transactions worked
Cash and accrual, matching and the adjusting entries
Revenue at a storage company: rent in advance, fees, concessions, protection plans
Receivables, the aging, the allowance and the lien sale
Fixed assets, depreciation and the register
Payables, Ramp cards, the bank reconciliation and cash controls
The close and the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement
Budgets, variance comments, internal controls and the audit

questions.q: Which statement answers 'did we make money this month'?
questions.explanation: The income statement covers a period; the balance sheet is a moment; the cash flow statement says where the cash went.

questions.q: A tenant pays December's rent on 11/28. In the November books that payment is:
questions.explanation: Nothing has been earned until December arrives. The company owes the tenant a month of storage.

questions.q: Which side increases an asset account?
questions.explanation: Debit increases assets and expenses; credit increases liabilities, equity and revenue.

questions.q: A vendor services the gate for $640; the invoice will be paid in two weeks. What is recorded now?
questions.explanation: Accrual books record the expense when the work was done and the payable until it is paid.

questions.q: Greens' financial statements are prepared on which basis?
questions.explanation: Accrual tells the truth about a month. The cash view is read beside it.

questions.q: Which of these are month-end adjusting entries? Pick all that apply.
questions.explanation: A card payment is an everyday transaction; the others move things into the right period at month end.

questions.q: Utilities are double the usual in November. The drill-down shows October's bill arrived late plus November's. This variance is:
questions.explanation: Two months' bills in one month is timing. It reverses on its own.

questions.q: The accounting equation is:
questions.explanation: Everything the business has was paid for by someone it owes or by its owners.

questions.q: What does the income statement report for rent?
questions.explanation: Earned rent: billed less concessions, for the period. The other three live on the operating reports.

questions.q: A free first month on a new garage is recorded as:
options: A reduction of revenue, with the reason
Nothing; it is not a transaction
questions.explanation: A concession reduces revenue and is recorded so leadership can see what was given away to rent units.

questions.q: Why does Accounting record an allowance for doubtful accounts each month?
options: Because the expected loss belongs in the same period as the revenue it came with
Because the lien law requires it
questions.explanation: Matching: the loss is recognized when the revenue is, not months later at the sale.

questions.q: A balance is written off after a lien sale. What expense is recorded at write-off?
options: Bad debt expense for the full balance
None; the expense was recorded when the allowance was built
questions.explanation: The write-off clears the receivable against the allowance. The expense already happened.

questions.q: A $3,800 replacement gate operator is:
options: A fixed asset that depreciates over its life
questions.explanation: It serves for years, so its cost is spread over them. A sprocket is a repair; an operator is capital.

questions.q: A gate operator cost $3,800 with a ten-year life. Monthly straight-line depreciation is about:
questions.explanation: $3,800 divided by 120 months.

questions.q: Why must a vendor invoice carry the ticket number?
options: So Accounting can match what was ordered, received and billed in one look; an unmatched invoice is not paid
So the site can pay it
questions.explanation: Three-way matching: the ticket, the inspection, the invoice.

questions.q: The bank reconciliation finds a $185 returned card payment. What does it mean?
options: A tenant's rent that Cubby recorded as paid bounced; the balance reopens and the desk calls
questions.explanation: Bank items the books missed are one of the three kinds of difference a reconciliation finds.

questions.q: Nexus keeps a second set of books for the sites.
questions.explanation: Greens keeps one set of books, in Intacct; Nexus reads it.

questions.q: Who at Greens reads the numbers? Pick all that apply.
questions.explanation: Each reader wants a different answer from the same books.

questions.q: Every amount on a Nexus Accounting report:
options: Drills down to the ledger lines that make it up, and each line to its transaction
Is rounded to the nearest thousand
questions.explanation: That trail is how a surprising number is checked.

questions.q: Which of these is a liability?
options: A security deposit a tenant paid
questions.explanation: The company holds the deposit and owes it back.

questions.q: Accounts numbered in the 4000s in a typical chart are:
questions.explanation: 1000s assets, 2000s liabilities, 3000s equity, 4000s revenue, 5000s and up expenses.

questions.q: Which account has a normal credit balance?
questions.explanation: Revenue grows on the credit side.

questions.q: Paying an invoice that was recorded two weeks ago does what?
options: Reduces accounts payable and reduces cash
questions.explanation: The expense was recorded when the work was done; paying it clears the liability and the cash.

questions.q: Wages earned this period but paid next period are recorded as:
options: Wages expense now and accrued payroll, a liability
questions.explanation: The expense belongs to the period the hours were worked.

questions.q: Under the cash basis, a repair done in October and paid in November counts in:
questions.explanation: Cash basis counts when the money moves. That is why it lies about a month.

questions.q: Matching means:
options: Revenue and the expenses that earned it fall in the same period
Every site gets the same budget
questions.explanation: Matching makes one month comparable to another.

questions.q: A storage site's rent is billed:
questions.explanation: The 1st is the biggest day in a storage company's books.

questions.q: Third-party tenant insurance collected with the rent is:
options: A liability until it is remitted to the insurer
questions.explanation: It is a pass-through. The protection plan, which is Greens' own program, is revenue.

questions.q: The gap between billed rent and collected rent is:
questions.explanation: Vacancy and rate separate potential from billed; concessions separate billed from earned; delinquency separates earned from collected.

questions.q: Lien sale proceeds are applied first to:
options: The vendor who cut the lock
questions.explanation: A lien sale is the end of a receivable, not a profit center; anything left over is owed to the tenant.

questions.q: A balance over 90 days on the aging report is:
options: Mostly gone; sold or written off soon
questions.explanation: The further right a balance sits, the less of it the company will ever see.

questions.q: The allowance for doubtful accounts is:
options: A contra asset that sits against receivables
questions.explanation: Receivables less the allowance is what the company really expects to collect.

questions.q: Which site habits shorten the aging report? Pick all that apply.
options: Running the lien process on schedule
questions.explanation: The site's habits set its bad debt.

questions.q: A former tenant pays $300 on a balance written off last year. It is recorded as:
questions.explanation: Never new rent.

questions.q: Land is depreciated over 39 years.
questions.explanation: Land never depreciates; the building on it does.

questions.q: Patching a roof section is usually:
questions.explanation: It keeps the asset working as it was. Replacing the whole roof is capital.

questions.q: Costs of a canopy project under construction sit in:
options: Construction in progress, until placed in service
questions.explanation: Depreciation begins when the asset is placed in service.

questions.q: Net book value is:
questions.explanation: A fully depreciated asset has a net book value near zero, which is one reason its replacement is a capital case.

questions.q: A storm destroys a canopy row. In the books:
options: Its net book value is written off and the insurance recovery is recorded against the loss
questions.explanation: The photos and the incident record are what the claim and the write-off rest on.

questions.q: Why is coding an invoice to the right entity important?
options: A miscoded invoice puts a cost on the wrong site's report
questions.explanation: Coding is the account plus the dimensions: entity, department, project.

questions.q: A Ramp card charge with no receipt:
options: Is an expense nobody can defend; it waits in suspense until explained
questions.explanation: The receipt is still the proof.

questions.q: Segregation of duties means:
options: Every site has its own accountant
No one person takes, records and reconciles the same cash
Vendors are paid by the site
questions.explanation: The first cash control.

questions.q: Which does a bank reconciliation find? Pick all that apply.
options: A deposit the bank posted the next day
A bank fee the books missed
questions.explanation: Timing differences, bank items and errors, including fraud.

questions.q: The storage industry values a site on:
questions.explanation: NOI is revenue less operating expenses, before financing and depreciation: the number a manager moves.

questions.q: Depreciation is added back on the cash flow statement because:
options: It was an expense that moved no cash
questions.explanation: The cash flow statement starts from net income and removes the non-cash items.

questions.q: A new roof appears on the cash flow statement under:
questions.explanation: Cash spent on assets is investing; loans and distributions are financing.

questions.q: Which close step comes first?
questions.explanation: Cut off, reconcile, revenue, payables and accruals, adjustments, review, lock.

questions.q: Economic occupancy is:
options: Rented units divided by total units
Earned rent divided by gross potential rent
questions.explanation: Potential actually collected, after vacancy, discounting and concessions.

questions.q: Net income flows into:
options: Retained earnings on the balance sheet
questions.explanation: That is how the income statement and the balance sheet connect.

questions.q: Which variance comment is useful?
options: Utilities $900 over: October's bill arrived in November, timing; November alone was on budget.
questions.explanation: What moved, why, timing or real, what next, with the numbers from the drill-down.

questions.q: Splitting a $9,000 job into two tickets to stay under a $5,000 limit is:
questions.explanation: Authorization limits are a control; a limit avoided is a control broken.

questions.q: Which records must exist for an audit? Pick all that apply.
options: Every vendor invoice with its ticket and approval
Every card charge with its receipt
questions.explanation: An audit follows trails. A site with complete records has nothing to prepare.

questions.q: What does an auditor do?
options: Tests: follows sample trails, confirms balances with outsiders, tests the controls and the judgments
questions.explanation: For a site an audit is a request for records that already exist.

questions.q: Records retention at a storage company is:
options: Set by law and policy and long; nothing is cleaned up
questions.explanation: Nexus keeps tickets, forms and Asset Management records by design; Cubby keeps the tenant side.

questions.q: A contra account:
options: Sits against another account to net it
questions.explanation: Accumulated depreciation against assets; the allowance against receivables.

questions.q: NOI margin is:
questions.explanation: How much of each rent dollar the site keeps after operating it.

questions.q: Cut-off is:
options: The line between one period's transactions and the next
questions.explanation: An invoice dated in the wrong month is a timing variance because of cut-off.

questions.q: An accrued expense is:
options: Incurred but not yet billed or paid
questions.explanation: Wages earned; the utility bill not yet in.

questions.q: A suspense account holds:
options: An uncoded or unexplained item until it is explained
questions.explanation: A card charge with no receipt waits there.

questions.q: Which is favorable?
questions.explanation: Over on revenue helps; over on expense hurts.

questions.q: Prepaid insurance is:
options: An asset used up a twelfth a month
questions.explanation: Paid ahead, expensed as the coverage is used.

questions.q: The person who takes payments at the site also reconciles the bank. This is:
questions.explanation: No one person takes, records and reconciles.

questions.q: Net operating income is before:
questions.explanation: NOI is the operating number; financing and depreciation sit below it.

questions.q: Prorated first-month rent is earned:
questions.explanation: Cubby prorates by its rule; the books follow it.
